significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish both a form-(iii) predictive coupling—an internally decoded "per-item CIE residual" predicts later misinformation reliance beyond stated belief—and a form-(ii) mechanism, since intervening on its carrier "reducing CIE-style errors" would causally connect the residual to behavior. This fixes a specific phenomenon, stated-belief/internal-belief dissociation after explicit retraction, and a consequential mechanism rather than merely showing that beliefs are decodable; Ecker et al. (2022, Nature Reviews Psychology) identifies continued influence after accepted corrections as the central explanatory signature of human CIE. A negative H1/H2 result would rule out this stale-linear-belief account, while failed localization alone would support only a distributed rather than modular account and therefore is less decisive. Topic-substitution check: replacing these retraction-specific predictions with the generic LLM-beliefs topic would not retain the predictive coupling or causal explanation and would merit only the topic median, so the claim-specific increment supports the higher score.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the claim's "per-item CIE residual" as a predictor and its "retraction-completion steering intervention" as a corrective knob. The predictor is ex ante: it is read after a correction but before the "downstream inference" whose failure it forecasts, leaving an action window for systems processing RAG updates or user retractions; the steering handle could then be used by auditors or deployment engineers rather than only by interpretability researchers. Re-extraction would be needed on each model, but the asserted relation—larger residual predicts continued reliance and explanatory-alternative retractions produce smaller residuals—still predicts what should be found across item types and LLMs, although the claim does not securely extend to very large closed models or unrelated belief changes. Topic-substitution check: generic research on LLM beliefs supplies neither this pre-inference warning signal nor the correction-specific intervention, so the reach score derives from the claim rather than the topic.
